analyzed_vuln.description: In the ASSIGN_OP var/tmpvar VM handler, the engine performs an in-place binary op (`zend_binary_op(var_ptr, var_ptr, value)`) and then unconditionally does `ZVAL_COPY(..., var_ptr)` when the result is used. For `/=` with string operands, `div_function()` may call `zval_ptr_dtor(result)` when `result == op1`, which frees the original string held by `var_ptr` before writing the numeric result. The handler still treats `var_ptr` as a valid source zval and increments refcount via `ZVAL_COPY`, causing a heap-use-after-free in `zend_gc_addref`. Root cause is stale pointer/state usage after in-place op mutates/frees op1, not `zend_gc_addref` itself.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger requires an ASSIGN_OP path handled by `ZEND_ASSIGN_OP_SPEC_VAR_TMPVAR_HANDLER` where return value is used (so `RETURN_VALUE_USED(opline)` is true) and the in-place op can destroy/rewrite the LHS zval storage (e.g., `/=` on a string value produced via prior concat/coercion). Fuzzed PHP code reaches this via execute harness, causing `zend_binary_op` -> `div_function` to dtor/free the old string, then handler copies from stale `var_ptr`, leading to UAF.
